aapl.notes: The segment note gives net sales and operating income by reporting geography. Apple reconciles the segment measure to consolidated operating income separately. Dollar amounts in these tables are millions unless amounts per share are specified.
aapl.request: An analyst attributes the change in consolidated operating income from fiscal 2023 to 2024 to higher sales. Prepare a symmetric bridge in USD millions. For each geographic segment, value its sales change at its average operating margin across the two years. Value its margin change at its average sales across those years. Use the resulting segment effects and the corporate reconciliation to explain the full consolidated change. Use signed contributions and the segment names as filed.
aapl.fields:
sales_effect = total contribution from changes in segment sales
margin_effect = total contribution from changes in within-segment margins
corporate_effect = contribution from the change in costs outside the segments
consolidated_change = actual change in consolidated operating income
largest_sales_drag = segment with the most negative sales contribution, as a string

msft.notes: Note 14 reports additional leases signed but not yet commenced at June 30, 2024. Operating commitments in that population were $8.6 billion and finance commitments $108.4 billion. They begin in fiscal years 2025 through 2030. Lease balances and the commitments schedule are reported in USD millions unless indicated. Use the filed table precision for calculations.
msft.request: Treasury is reconciling the FY2025 lease payment budget to the balance sheet at June 30, 2024. Test these claims against the documentation. A. The aggregate commitments line includes imputed interest. B. The current liabilities for the two lease classes sum to the first year of their maturity schedules. C. The cash-payment excess in FY2025 of the aggregate commitments schedule over the two Note 14 maturity schedules is entirely attributable to finance leases. D. The two Note 14 maturity totals reconcile to the recognized operating and finance lease liabilities after removing imputed interest. Include only claims established by the supplied disclosures.
msft.fields:
supported = JSON list of the supported letter IDs, in alphabetical order
fy2025_excess = FY2025 aggregate lease commitments less the two Note 14 cash maturities, in USD millions
interest = combined imputed interest removed from the undiscounted Note 14 totals, positive USD millions
current_gap = FY2025 cash maturities for both classes in Note 14 less their recognized current lease liabilities, in USD millions

goog.notes: The severance expense includes cash-settled involuntary termination benefits and stock-based compensation. The liability rollforward omits $432 million of noncash stock compensation. Its closing amount is included in accrued compensation and benefits. All figures in the note tables are USD millions.
goog.request: Audit these assertions about Alphabet’s 2023 cost actions. A. More than half of all 2023 severance expense was allocated to research and development. B. Cash paid in 2023 exceeded 90% of the charges that entered the severance liability. C. The disclosures establish the exact amount of noncash stock compensation charged specifically to sales and marketing as part of this action. D. The closing severance liability equals the portion of expense neither paid in cash nor charged as stock compensation in 2023. Include only claims established by the supplied disclosures.
goog.fields:
supported = JSON list of supported letter IDs in alphabetical order
cash_settled_pct = cash paid as a percentage of charges entering the severance liability
rd_share_pct = research and development as a percentage of all severance expense
expense_less_cash = total severance expense less cash paid, in USD millions
closing_liability = year-end severance liability, in USD millions

nflx.notes: An agreement for a future title can create a commitment before recognition as a content liability. Availability of the title triggers liability recognition for acquired or licensed titles. The maturity table includes known minimum amounts. Future titles of indeterminate number or price can create additional obligations. Management estimated roughly $1 billion to $4 billion beyond the table over the next three years, with the vast majority of that range expected after the first twelve months. These amounts are estimates. The filed tables use USD thousands.
nflx.request: Review the content risk disclosure as of December 31, 2023. A. Obligations due after three years represent less than 15% of total tabulated content commitments. B. Management’s upper estimate of additional commitments for unknown titles is already included in the maturity total. C. The exact portion of those additional commitments that will be paid within twelve months can be calculated. D. Recognized content liabilities are less than half of total tabulated content obligations. Report only claims supported by the records. Compute the amounts from the detailed tables.
nflx.fields:
supported = JSON list of supported letter IDs in alphabetical order
recognized = current plus noncurrent recognized content liabilities in USD thousands
unrecognized_known = tabulated content obligations outside recognized content liabilities, in USD thousands
after_three_years_pct = share of tabulated content obligations due after three years, in percent
upper_scenario = tabulated content obligations plus the upper estimate of additional commitments, in USD millions

luv.notes: Southwest’s operating statistics include reported fuel volume and rounded per-gallon prices. Its special-items reconciliation provides fuel expense on GAAP and economic bases. The derivative note identifies where premium expense or benefit appears in earnings. The fuel-expense reconciliation and its signed adjustments use USD millions. Fuel volumes are millions of gallons.
luv.request: Decompose the change in economic fuel expense from 2022 to 2023 in USD millions. Use expense divided by reported fuel gallons to derive the price each year. Value the incremental gallons at the earlier price, then apply the price change to the later volume. Also explain the difference between the economic and GAAP year-over-year changes using the signed adjustments. Within the economic-versus-GAAP bridge distinguish the 2023-minus-2022 contribution from premiums on contracts not designated as hedges.
luv.fields:
volume = signed economic expense effect from the volume movement
price = signed economic expense effect from the price movement
economic_change = signed total economic fuel expense change
basis_difference = economic change minus GAAP fuel expense change
premium_contribution = contribution from the nondesignated premium adjustment to basis_difference

nvda.notes: In Note 10, NVIDIA reports that inventory provisions charged to cost of revenue were $774 million in fiscal 2024 and $1.0 billion in fiscal 2023. Dollar tables are in millions except for per-share amounts. The two balance-sheet dates delimit the fiscal 2024 measurement period.
nvda.request: For fiscal 2024, estimate how inventory days and gross margin would differ in a one-period sensitivity. Assume the 2024 inventory provision had not been taken, its entire amount would still have been in inventory at period end, and all other revenue, expenses, opening balances and asset movements would be unchanged. Define days as average opening and closing inventory divided by annual cost of revenue times the actual number of days between the two fiscal closing dates. Use the unrounded income-statement figures to compute the change in gross margin.
nvda.fields:
days_in_period = actual elapsed days
reported_inventory_days = inventory days at the reported amounts
scenario_inventory_days = inventory days under the sensitivity
margin_lift_bps = scenario gross margin less reported gross margin, in basis points
reported_wip_change = closing work in process less prior year-end work in process, in USD millions

amzn.notes: Amazon’s equipment-based free-cash-flow measure counts equipment acquired under finance leases and principal repayments on the other finance leases. The equipment addition is a subset of all property and equipment acquired under finance leases shown in supplemental cash flows. The other-finance-lease repayments are a subset of total finance-lease principal payments. Tables use USD millions. These are separate measures defined by the issuer.
amzn.request: Compare Amazon’s alternative cash flow measures for calendar 2023, then determine how their spread changed from 2022. Assess four claims. A. Substituting the entire supplementary property-and-equipment figure for the equipment figure leaves the equipment-based measure unchanged. B. Principal repayments of financing obligations enter both measures. C. Relative to the principal-repayment measure, the equipment measure replaces just the principal repayments attributable to equipment with current equipment acquisitions. D. The spread between the two measures widened in 2023. Include only statements supported by the filing.
amzn.fields:
supported = JSON list of supported letter IDs in alphabetical order
equipment_principal = principal repayments attributable to equipment in 2023, positive USD millions
equipment_additions = equipment additions charged in the equipment-based measure in 2023, positive USD millions
spread_2023 = equipment-based measure less principal-repayment measure in 2023, signed USD millions
spread_change = 2023 spread less 2022 spread, signed USD millions

ford.notes: Note 17 presents U.S. pension, non-U.S. pension and worldwide other postemployment benefit plans separately. Its pension figures include funded and unfunded plans. A distinct management summary reports both all plans and a subset of funded plans in USD billions rounded to one decimal place. Use the note’s USD million figures for computations.
ford.request: Reconcile the change from 2022 to 2023 in global pension funded status (plan assets less benefit obligation). Management wants a bridge for the full pension population. For 2023 also compute a constant-currency, no-amendment scenario: set only the 2023 foreign-exchange translation and plan amendment movements to zero, keeping all other movements as reported in both assets and obligations. Treat the U.S. and non-U.S. plans as one pool. Retain signs for surpluses, deficits, and contributions.
ford.fields:
actual_end = global pension funded status at end of 2023, USD millions
actual_change = change from end of 2022, USD millions
fx_effect = 2023 signed contribution of translation to the actual funded-status change, USD millions
amendment_effect = signed contribution of 2023 plan amendments to the actual change, USD millions
scenario_change = change from the actual 2022 opening comparison to the adjusted 2023 closing funded status, USD millions
